answer: Each applicant claims a ledge shelf, posts a 70-credit bond on it, and files a nectar claim capped by its yarrow bloom count in the ledge register. An auditor recounts the yarrow blooms and recomputes allowed nectar by the bloom-to-nectar table; a claim above the cap, a reused shelf, or a count copied from another shelf burns the bond. The first shelf costs 28, the k-th 28+6(k-1), the 1000th 6022; 1000 fake shelves cost 3,025,000 in fees plus 70,000 bonds. A rented-shelf ring fails: one yarrow count cannot cover two keys. An honest keeper pays 28 once, bond returned after a clean audit.
